body: claimed: issue worker (Opus) · 2026-11-18T14:58Z · worktree/branch issue/2543-main-red-posts · plan: find the merge that broke each of the 4 tests and repair it

Causes found. No failure is wrong posted G-code.

1. `first_router_part_posts_the_shipped_program`: #2504 (merge 90e016a6e) saved `examples/first-router-part.camproj` at v68 with `"break_through_from": "full_diameter"`. The posted drill depth is now `Z-14.803`, not `Z-13`. The difference, 1.803 mm, is the point of the Ø6 118° drill. #2488 (merge c9b1366ac) added the pin of `examples/first-router-part.nc` at the same time. Each PR did not include the change of the other. Old project files without the key still load as `tip` (`settle_drill_break_through`), so they keep their depth.
2. `thread_boss` and `thread_mill`: #2488 gives each tool a number at `AddTool`, in the order of addition. The fixtures add the thread mill first, so it is now `T01`. Only the tool comment, the `T` word and the `H` word change. Each operation calls its own tool with the matching `H` word.
3. ui `demo_projects_build_and_load_with_valid_paths`: the gate log shows `save /tmp/camcraft-guide-projects/guide-workholding.camproj: I/O error: Permission denied (os error 13)`. The test writes to a fixed directory in the shared temp directory. Another account on the runner owns it. This failure is older than 4cab68f97: runs 44285991575, 44296963679 and 44302217388 show it too. It came with #1902 (c92a1cb2e).

Plan: record the three programs again, and write the ui demo projects to a directory of the test process.

Cause found for 1-3, by a local run of the same tree (main at 8643d9bb7 plus two test lines):

1. `first_router_part_posts_the_shipped_program`: `examples/first-router-part.nc` is stale. #2504 moved the `Drill1` depths (`Z-14.803`), and #2488 changed tool numbers; the shipped `.nc` in the `examples/` of the merged tree does not match what posting now gives. The test says: regenerate it.
2. `thread_boss` and `thread_mill`: their goldens (`crates/app/tests/golden/nc/thread_mill_external_m8_multi_form.nc`, `thread_mill_m8_multi_form.nc`) still carry the old tool numbers (#2488 stable tool numbers: the same operations now post `T01`/`T02`, the goldens say `T03`/`T01`). No G-code other than the `T`/`H` words differs - the moves are byte-equal. Regenerate with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1`, or take the numbers the fixture order now gives.
3. `guide_projects`: not a golden problem. The test passes locally when its suite runs alone. On the gate the whole `camcraft-ui` lib runs at 6 threads, and these tests share one temp directory (`%TEMP%/camcraft-guide-projects`): `write_all_demo_projects` rewrites the three `.camproj` files while another test loads them. The failure is a race, and it is old (it failed on three runs before #2499 and #2488 too). Fix: one directory per test (for example `temp_dir().join(format!("camcraft-guide-projects-{}", std::process::id()))`), or a shared `Once` fixture. I am confirming with a full-suite local run and will edit this comment with the result.

Not caused by #2531, #2530, #2534, #2465, #2460, #2513 or #2522.

Update on item 3 (`guide_projects`): the race theory did not confirm. A full `camcraft-ui` lib run on this machine on this tree: 1156 passed, 0 failed, in 41 s, with the tests in their normal thread pool. The local single-run result is green every time so far; the gate run is red. What differs on the gate runner: the temp directory survives from run to run, and each step runs with `--test-threads=6`. Next check: the same run on the gate runner label, and a check whether an old `guide-*.camproj` left in `%TEMP%/camcraft-guide-projects` by an earlier build can answer `load_noted` with a note. I will edit item 3 here when that answers.

Evidence from mkinney's release dry run on the same commit `8643d9bb7` (`cargo xtask gate release --no-snapshots`, 16-vCPU Linux cloud server, 52.7 min, 1104 steps, 6 failed). It has the assert texts that the post-merge log does not show, and two release-only failures that the batch tier cannot see:

1. `first_part_programs::first_router_part_posts_the_shipped_program`: `examples/first-router-part.nc is stale; compare /tmp/camcraft-first-router-part-program-pin-*.nc and regenerate it`.
2. `thread_boss::an_external_m8_thread_verifies_clean_and_posts_helical_moves`: `golden tests/golden/nc/thread_mill_external_m8_multi_form.nc is stale`.
3. `thread_mill::a_multi_form_mill_threads_m8_clean_and_posts_helical_moves`: `golden tests/golden/nc/thread_mill_m8_multi_form.nc is stale`. (Posted G-code: each changed line must be explained before a golden moves.)
4. **Release only** - `camcraft-motion` lib (heavy, `--ignored --release`): `machining2d::pocket_hsm::ring_tests::the_stock_ring_level_plans_adaptive_with_no_budget_note` and its sibling `ring_tests` test.
5. **Release only** - app heavy `pocket3d_hsm::the_users_whole_model_bore_roughs_adaptive_on_each_level` (`pocket3d_hsm.rs:171`): `every level keeps the HSM plan: ["adaptive: the HSM plan cut from the air would cut 19.2% of D at (26.59, -22.76), over the 14.6% optimal load by 31% - Offset rings cut the level at Z 15.000 instead", ...]`. Items 4 and 5 are both in the adaptive stock-ring budget (#2035 area).
6. ui lib `setup_mount_pages::each_setup_picks_its_own_machine_and_post_and_posts_one_file_per_mount`: `Harness::run exceeded max_steps (4)` (a scroll-area repaint). The same test failed the same way on `199314e23` on a fresh cloud server and passed on two other machines, so it may be deterministic on a clean Linux checkout rather than flaky.

Full logs are kept on M5; we can attach any of them. We did not change anything (mkinney's pools now work only on mkinney's own PRs).
